Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 14:00 - 14:44 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Avery Cole (Brightmoor Head of AI), Marcus Lim (Eng Manager), Sana Patel (Infra Lead), Evan Zhou (Procurement)
summary: Check-in focused on Brightmoor's renewal window (June 2026) and planned capacity uplift. Discussed adding EU and APAC reserved nodes, latency targets for checkout flows, data residency constraints, and contract amendment path. Action items set for pricing, latency tests, and procurement timeline alignment.
topics: Capacity uplift sizing for EU and APAC
Latency SLOs for customer-facing checkout use-case
Private deployment and data residency considerations
Pricing and billing cadence for reserved capacity
questions: What is the expected go-live date for EU nodes?
Can Redwood provide KMS/HSM integration details for on-prem keys?
How does automatic fallback to hosted variants work during regional maintenance windows?
transcript:
[00:00] Carlos Mendez: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Carlos from Redwood, AE. We've got Priya, our solutions engineer. How's it going on your side Avery?
[00:06] Avery Cole: Good, thanks. Morning for us. We wanted to run through the uplift plan, make sure renewal timing still lines up with our budget window in June.
[00:14] Priya Nair: Hi all. I'll try to keep the technical bits concrete — sizing numbers, what tests we recommend.
[00:19] Marcus Lim: Quick note, procurement's asked us to tighten the latency target for checkout — they want p95 < 280ms not 350. Is that feasible with EU nodes?
[00:28] Priya Nair: p95 < 280ms is tight but possible. Depends on model footprint, batching, and whether you use Dedicated GPU pools versus hosted fallbacks. If you pin to dedicated capacity in eu-west, we can meet that with the right batching profile.
[00:41] Sana Patel: Is there any change to the KV cache behavior across regions? We saw cache misses spike in our last APAC pilot.
[00:48] Priya Nair: Good point — cross-region cache warming is tricky. The runtime uses prefix/K V cache strategies; if you split traffic by routing policy to region-local pools, cache hit rate improves. If you fail over to other regions, you'll see misses until KV warms. There's also an optional shared warm-start snapshot we can schedule during cutovers.
[01:04] Evan Zhou: Can we get that in writing? Procurement will want the failover behaviour documented for the contract.
[01:09] Carlos Mendez: Absolutely — we'll include the failover playbook in the addendum.
[01:13] Avery Cole: Our timeline: want EU nodes live by late July, APAC pilot in September. Renewal signature ideally mid-June. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[01:22] Priya Nair: For EU by late July we need the sizing confirmation and network prep by May 3rd. Also need KMS details if you're bringing your own keys. 
[01:32] Marcus Lim: On KMS — we run with AWS KMS and have an internal HSM for some PII flows. How does Redwood Private support that?
[01:40] Priya Nair: Our Private deployment supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations — we can plug into your VPC and handshake with your key policy. There are a couple of options: full on-prem package or VPC-private control plane with customer KMS. We can share the integration doc. Note, the on-prem package has longer lead time for provisioning.
[01:58] Avery Cole: Do we need an on-prem package for EU? Data residency says no cross-border storage of raw logs, so VPC with managed control plane should be fine if logs can be kept in-region.
[02:09] Priya Nair: Yes if you can enforce region-local logging and KMS keys, you can avoid the on-prem path. We'll document the retention controls and audit log exports.
[02:19] Marcus Lim: Can we talk about pricing? We're looking at a committed uplift of roughly 2.5x current reserved capacity for peak season. How does that affect rate cards for EU and APAC?
[02:29] Carlos Mendez: We'll draft a tiered pricing table — baseline reserved units, burst pool pricing, and per-token for overflow. EU and APAC have region premiums based on hardware and availability. I'll send a detailed table by Friday.
[02:40] Evan Zhou: For procurement, we also need SLA credits and rollback windows.
[02:44] Carlos Mendez: We'll put standard SLA language and a proposed credit schedule into the amendment. If you want a stricter latency SLA for checkout, we can add a performance-based clause.
[02:55] Avery Cole: That would be helpful — performance-based credits tied to p95 for model X in checkout path.
[03:01] Priya Nair: We'll need to instrument traces at the route level. The Console can give you per-route token/latency breakdowns. We also recommend a two-hour controlled stress test on the existing setup to collect baseline before we size the Dedicated nodes.
[03:15] Marcus Lim: Can Redwood run that test or do we need to?
[03:18] Priya Nair: We can run it if you give us a test window and temporary credentials; otherwise we can provide a script for you to run. The results need to include p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost estimations.
[03:30] Marcus Lim: We'll probably run it ourselves but would like Redwood to validate the results.
[03:34] Priya Nair: Totally fair.
[03:36] [04:00] Speaker 2 (unlabeled): [laughs] sorry, just jumping in — did you mean 2.5x committed?
[04:05] Avery Cole: Yes, 2.5x committed. Peak events drive that.
[04:08] Priya Nair: A 2.5x uplift usually maps to a mix of reserved plus a small burst pool. For cost optimization we suggest: 1) reserve main capacity in EU, 2) use autoscale burst in APAC for unpredictable spikes, 3) enable prefix caching aggressively for repeated queries and rerank flows.
[04:26] Sana Patel: How does rollback work if a rollout causes regressions? We had a rollout last quarter that impacted latency.
[04:32] Priya Nair: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies by model variant. You can pin traffic, do a 5% canary, and if latency or quality regressions occur, the system will auto-fallback to the previous variant or an alternate compatible model. We'll include a canary recipe in the playbook.
[04:47] Marcus Lim: On the canary we also want alerting hooked into PagerDuty. Is the tracing compatible?
[04:53] Priya Nair: Yes Console has tracing hooks and integrates with common alerting tools. We'll provide a sample Prometheus/Grafana dashboard and PD integration steps.
[05:02] Evan Zhou: From legal side, we need the termination terms updated if we add Dedicated nodes in EU — specifically a 90-day exit window if capacity commitments change. Is that feasible?
[05:12] Carlos Mendez: Typically commitments are on a 12/24 month cadence but we can add an amendment that defines a staged exit with prorated refunds. I'll loop in contracts to craft language.
[05:22] Avery Cole: Is there any known maintenance window for Dedicated clusters that would affect peak times? We can't have maintenance during our Black Friday windows.
[05:30] Priya Nair: We have configurable maintenance windows; Dedicated clusters can align with your blackout windows. For mission-critical peaks we recommend secondary failover regions to avoid single-region maintenance impacting traffic.
[05:45] Avery Cole: Can you clarify the failover latency penalty? If we fail to another region, how much higher should we expect p95 to go?
[05:53] Priya Nair: For cross-region failover expect additional network latency — ballpark add 80–200ms depending on geography. Also KV miss rate will increase so model response times might take a small hit. We can measure your specific footprint in the stress test.
[06:08] Marcus Lim: For the EU nodes: what hardware are we looking at? A100 or H100?
[06:14] Priya Nair: We recommend H100 for large gen models and A100 for mid-sized convos. For your checkout model, H100 gives headroom at peak but increases unit cost. We'll show hardware + quantization options in the pricing pack.
[06:27] Carlos Mendez: Quick recap before we go into logistics: Brightmoor wants EU by late July, APAC pilot Sept, renewal mid-June. Carlos will send pricing and SLA addendum by 2026-04-16. Priya will run / validate a 2-hour latency/throughput stress test and share results by 2026-04-20. Brightmoor to confirm procurement timeline and data residency specifics by 2026-04-21.
[06:48] Avery Cole: Sounds good. One more question: are there any limits on model versions we can pin? We want to pin a frozen variant for checkout flows.
[06:56] Priya Nair: You can pin model versions and rollout policies. Keep in mind pinning means you won't automatically get runtime performance improvements from newer kernels; you'll need a planned migration path. We can manage that with staged rollouts.
[07:09] Sana Patel: Ok, for the stress test, I'll coordinate a window next week and share credentials with Priya.
[07:16] Priya Nair: Great, thank you.
[07:18] Evan Zhou: From procurement, once we get pricing and SLAs we'll aim to have legal review by May 10.
[07:25] Carlos Mendez: Noted — I'll aim to get everything crisp for your review.
[07:29] [07:45] Carlos Mendez: Anything else before we wrap?
[07:48] Avery Cole: No, that's it. Thanks for the quick sync.
[07:51] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and test plan.
[07:55] Carlos Mendez: Thanks — talk soon.
[08:00] [meeting end — 14:44 UTC]

Notes on transcript: occasional speaker attribution may be imprecise; some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV cache sometimes written as K V cache). There were short cross-talk segments and a couple of inaudible words marked with [inaudible].
